newsitem.title: CHINA: China says U.S. poultry ban limited to two states. [CORRECTED 4:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: China says U.S. poultry ban limited to two states. [CORRECTED 4:30 GMT]

text.p: China's ban on imports of U.S. poultry and poultry products applies only to imports from the two American states affected by an outbreak of viscerotropic velogenic Newcastle Disease (clarifying disease), Chinese officials said on Tuesday.
An official of the Ministry of Agriculture told Reuters that the ban is already in effect.
The ban covers poultry from the U.S. states of Missouri and Oklahoma, the ministry official said.
Earlier, the official Xinhua news agency said that the ban affected all poultry imported from the United States.
The official said, however, that China had banned all U.S. poultry brought into the country either by mail or hand-carried by travellers.
"Travellers are barred from bringing in any poultry goods from the United States," he said. "These products also cannot be brought into China through the mail."
He described the move as aimed at preventing damage from a "very destructive disease".
An official of the State Bureau of Animal Plant and Quarantine said the ban went into effect on Monday.
He told Reuters that the action was unrelated to other trade disputes with the United States and there was no plan to delay implementation of the decision.
Beijing and Washington are also at odds over textile imports, and that dispute has threatened to spill over into the farm sector.
China had threatened to ban some U.S. farm goods -- as well as textiles and alcoholic drinks -- in retaliation for U.S. penalties on textiles purchased from China.

On Sunday, Beijing announced it was delaying for one month the implementation of those restrictions, which had been scheduled to take effect today, as the two sides were planning to hold further talks on the issue.
